## What the body quietly admits

Besides mood surveys, labs track signals you might never notice yourself.

**Heart rate variability (HRV)** — how much the gap between beats varies; higher often means calmer "rest-and-digest" tone. **Pupil size** — pupils widen with sympathetic arousal. **Skin conductance** — tiny sweat changes from stress [^1]. **Vessel tone** — how tight or relaxed blood vessels are.

Tea patterns in the packs often look calmer than coffee alone; alcohol often looks worse for these control signals.

Think of HRV as how flexibly your heart "breathes" between beats when you are calm versus locked tight when you are stressed. Skin conductance is like a tiny stress sweat meter you cannot feel but a lab can [^1].

| Measure | Plain meaning | Tea / caffeine / alcohol pattern in the packs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heart rate variability (HRV) | How much the gap between beats varies; higher often means calmer "rest-and-digest" tone | Tea linked with higher high-frequency HRV; coffee and alcohol tend to lower HRV |
| Pupil size | Pupils widen with sympathetic arousal | Caffeine can dilate; alcohol can slow the light reflex |
| Skin conductance | Tiny sweat changes from stress | Coffee can spike it; tea often keeps it steadier |
| Vessel tone | How tight or relaxed blood vessels are | Caffeine can constrict cerebral vessels; L-theanine may counteract via nitric oxide pathways [^2] |

Example numbers from the packs:

- **200 mg L-theanine** during mental arithmetic: heart-rate and stress-marker reductions consistent with less sympathetic drive; one common HRV index up about **15.4 ± 3.2 ms** in the pack narrative of Kimura-linked work [^3].  
- **150 mg caffeine** in attention tasks: mean pupil diameter up about **0.42 ± 0.08 mm** (Wetzel et al., 2016; pack).  
- **200 mg L-theanine + 100 mg caffeine** under stress: skin conductance up only about **0.15 ± 0.04 µS** vs about **+0.88 µS** for caffeine alone (Rogers et al., 2008) [^4].  

Besides mood, these signals help researchers say "calmer control" with numbers. In these sources, higher HRV during hard thinking is also read as better top-down control—less impulsive, better emotional regulation.

People sometimes shrug: "HRV is only a fitness score." In these sources, higher HRV during hard thinking is also read as better top-down control. L-theanine is described as protecting that balance; coffee or alcohol often reduce it.

Notice how the wired feeling has a skin signature too: caffeine-driven alert patterns line up with higher skin conductance (about **+0.88 µS** for caffeine alone in one comparison) [^4]. Feeling "wired" is not only a mood word.

Matched tea-constituent drinks in Rogers and colleagues' design—*Time for tea*—are also a bridge into Chapter 4's protocol talk: same volume, controlled temperature, and timed cognitive tests after drinking [^4].

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="More detail: HRV, pupils, and skin conductance numbers"}
| Measure | Plain meaning | Pattern in these packs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HRV | Beat-to-beat flexibility; higher often = calmer "rest-and-digest" tone | Tea / L-theanine linked with higher HF-HRV or RMSSD under load; coffee and alcohol tend to lower HRV |
| Pupil size | Widens with sympathetic arousal | Caffeine can dilate; alcohol can slow the light reflex |
| Skin conductance | Tiny stress-sweat changes | Coffee can spike it; tea often steadier |
| Vessel tone | Constriction vs relaxation | Caffeine can constrict cerebral vessels; L-theanine may counteract via NO pathways[^2] |

Example numbers:

- **200 mg L-theanine** during mental arithmetic: HR / stress-marker reductions; one common HRV index up about **15.4 ± 3.2 ms** in the pack narrative of Kimura-linked work.[^3]
- **150 mg caffeine** in attention tasks: mean pupil diameter up about **0.42 ± 0.08 mm** (Wetzel et al., 2016; pack).
- **200 mg L-theanine + 100 mg caffeine** under stress: skin conductance up only about **0.15 ± 0.04 µS** vs about **+0.88 µS** for caffeine alone.[^4]

Higher HRV during hard thinking is also read as better top-down control—less impulsive, better emotional regulation—not only a "fitness score."[^3] Feeling "wired" has a skin signature too: that ~**+0.88 µS** caffeine-alone bump is measurable arousal, not only a mood word.[^4]
:::
